items.example_en: Our flat is on the third floor.
items.note: 楼 is the measure for floors: 三楼 is the third floor.

items.example_en: We always eat in the kitchen.
items.note: 房 recurs in room words: 厨房, 书房, 房间.

items.example_en: The bedroom faces the courtyard.
items.note: 房间 is any room.

items.example_en: The toilet is at the end of the corridor.
items.note: Literally hand-washing room, the polite public term. 厕所 is blunter.

items.example_en: We're watching a film in the living room.
items.note: Literally guest hall.

items.example_en: There are lots of plants on the balcony.
items.note: 上 after a noun makes it a location: 阳台上.

items.example_en: The keys are on the table.
items.note: 在 plus place plus 上: the location suffix is obligatory.

items.example_en: The cat is sleeping under the bed.
items.note: Its measure word is 张: 一张床.

items.example_en: Hang the coat in the wardrobe.
items.note: 把 moves the object before the verb when you dispose of it somehow.

items.example_en: The lamp is next to the sofa.
items.note: Position words follow the noun, unlike English prepositions.

items.example_en: The bakery is opposite my place.
We're moving at the end of the month.
items.note: Verb-object compound: 搬 to move plus 家 home.

items.example_en: I get up at seven.
items.note: The time goes before the verb: 七点起床, never 起床七点.

items.example_en: I often wake up as early as six.
items.note: 就 signals that the speaker finds it early or sooner than expected.

items.example_en: I shower before going out.
items.note: 前 comes after the clause it applies to: 出门前.

items.example: 快穿衣服，五分钟后出发。
items.example_en: Get dressed quickly, we're leaving in five minutes.
items.note: 穿 for clothes and shoes; 戴 for glasses, hats, jewellery.

items.example_en: I cycle to work.
items.note: 下班 is to finish work. The means of transport comes first.

items.example_en: I go to bed around midnight.
items.note: Verb-object compound, so 睡了三个小时觉 splits it.

items.example: 我们星期六早上打扫房间。
items.example_en: We clean the flat on Saturday mornings.
You cook, I'll wash the dishes.
items.note: 碗 is a bowl, and stands in for dishes generally.

items.example_en: I do the laundry on Sundays.
Don't forget to take out the rubbish.
items.note: 别 plus verb is the everyday negative command.

items.example_en: I usually have lunch at twelve.
items.note: Goes before the verb, like all adverbs.

items.example_en: I occasionally do some sport.
items.note: Family: 经常 often, 有时候 sometimes, 从来不 never.

items.example: 我想找一件冬天的外套。
items.example_en: I'm looking for a winter coat.
items.note: 件 is the measure word for clothes.

items.example: 我喜欢这件毛衣，可以试试吗？
items.example_en: I like this jumper, can I try it on?
items.note: Doubling a verb softens it: 试试 means give it a quick try.

items.example_en: Do you have the next size up?
items.note: 号 also works: 大号, 中号, 小号.

items.example_en: The fitting rooms are at the back.
items.note: 间 marks rooms: 试衣间, 洗手间, 房间.

items.english: it fits well, it suits me
items.example_en: This colour suits me well.
items.note: 合适 is suitable; 适合 is the verb to suit.

items.example_en: Great, I'll take this one.
items.note: 要 covers want, will have, and need.

items.example_en: Forty yuan is too expensive.
items.note: 便宜 is cheap. 太 ... 了 is the standard frame.

items.example_en: These are all on sale.
items.note: 打八折 means twenty percent OFF, not eighty. The number is what you pay.

items.example_en: Can I pay by card?
items.note: In practice most people pay by phone: 手机支付.

items.example_en: Do you need an official receipt?
items.note: A tax document, distinct from 收据, a plain receipt.

items.example_en: Keep the change.
items.note: Same 找 as in to look for: the shop looks for your change.

items.example_en: We're saving money for a trip.
items.note: Also to deposit money at a bank.
